title: Tirumala Tirupati Darshan: A First Timer's Planning Guide
intro: A visit to Tirumala is a long awaited trip for many families. Some advance planning makes the day calmer. This guide covers the basics.

p: Darshan tickets and accommodation are available on the official TTD website and app. Avoid unofficial agents and brokers, who may overcharge or sell fake bookings.
There are free darshan queues and paid special entry options. Waiting times vary a great deal, with weekends and festivals the busiest. Weekdays are generally calmer.
Traditional dress is expected. Mobile phones and bags are usually not allowed inside the queue complexes, so check the latest rules and lockers before you go.
You can drive or take a bus up the ghat road, or walk the Alipiri or Srivari Mettu footpaths, which many devotees take as a vow. Carry water and wear comfortable shoes if you walk.
Keep identity proofs for everyone, since they are checked. Take care of children and elders during long waits. Allow a full day, and keep time for the nearby temples such as Tiruchanur.

faq.a: As early as booking opens, since slots fill quickly, especially in festival months.
Rules change, so check the current TTD guidelines before travelling.

disclaimer: Note: rules and charges change. Please check the official TTD website before travelling.
